papers.title: NF106: A Neurofibromatosis Clinical Trials Consortium Phase II Trial of the MEK Inhibitor Mirdametinib (PD-0325901) in Adolescents and Adults With NF1-Related Plexiform Neurofibromas.
papers.summary: In this 19-patient phase II trial, mirdametinib produced partial volumetric shrinkage of inoperable plexiform neurofibromas in 42% of adolescents and adults with neurofibromatosis type 1 and was generally tolerable, although acneiform rash, fatigue, nausea, pain, and dose reductions were common. Tumor pain intensity decreased, but quality-of-life findings were exploratory and mixed, and small sample size, lack of dose optimization, early removal of nonresponders, and absent post-treatment MRI limited assessment of efficacy and durability.
papers.why: This phase II trial directly demonstrated mirdametinib activity in NF1-associated plexiform neurofibromas using volumetric MRI and pain outcomes.

papers.title: Treatment decisions and the use of MEK inhibitors for children with neurofibromatosis type 1-related plexiform neurofibromas.
papers.summary: This review identifies selumetinib as the only approved medical therapy for pediatric neurofibromatosis type 1 with symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibroma and summarizes trials showing tumor shrinkage and improvements in pain, quality of life, strength, and range of motion. It also evaluates investigational MEK inhibitors, cabozantinib, surgery, volumetric MRI, and treatment-selection methods, while emphasizing unresolved long-term efficacy, safety, and sequencing questions.
papers.why: This review provides tested and investigational treatment options for NF1-related plexiform neurofibroma together with relevant clinical response and patient-reported outcome measures.

papers.title: Case report: Treatment response of NF-1-associated bladder ganglioneuroma to trametinib.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 4-year-old girl with neurofibromatosis type 1-associated unresectable urinary bladder ganglioneuroma whose symptoms and tumor extent improved during trametinib treatment after sirolimus had failed. The findings support trametinib, a MEK inhibitor targeting RAS/MAPK signaling, as a potential therapy for this rare NF1-associated neoplasm, although evidence is limited to one patient.
papers.why: Reports clinical and radiographic response of an NF1-associated bladder ganglioneuroma to trametinib after failure of sirolimus.

papers.title: Lamotrigine for cognitive deficits associated with neurofibromatosis type 1: A phase II randomized placebo-controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a phase II randomized placebo-controlled trial, 26 weeks of lamotrigine did not improve performance IQ or most secondary neurocognitive outcomes in adolescents with neurofibromatosis type 1. Visual sustained attention showed a non-significant trend toward improvement, but the small, underpowered study and lack of multiplicity correction do not support a treatment effect, although lamotrigine was generally well tolerated.
papers.why: A randomized placebo-controlled NF1 trial directly tested lamotrigine with standardized cognitive and electrophysiological outcomes and found no meaningful cognitive benefit.

papers.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Pilot Study of N-Acetylcysteine for Motor and Cognitive Symptoms in Youth With Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
papers.summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial evaluated oral N-acetylcysteine (NAC) for motor, behavioral, cognitive, and biomarker outcomes in children and adolescents with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). NAC was generally well tolerated but did not improve the primary motor outcome or any secondary or exploratory outcome at 8 weeks; two participants were withdrawn because of worsening behavior.
papers.why: A randomized placebo-controlled trial directly tested N-acetylcysteine in youth with NF1 and provided motor, cognitive, safety, and exploratory biomarker outcomes, although it found no significant efficacy.

papers.title: Photodynamic Therapy for Benign Cutaneous Neurofibromas Using Aminolevulinic Acid Topical Application and 633 nm Red Light Illumination.
papers.summary: This phase I clinical trial found that microneedle-assisted topical aminolevulinic acid was preferentially converted to protoporphyrin IX within cutaneous neurofibromas, and subsequent 633 nm photodynamic therapy induced apoptosis and inflammation in treated tumors. A maximum tolerable light dose of 100 J/cm2 was established, but treatment caused substantial pain and did not significantly reduce lesion size or growth during limited follow-up.
papers.why: A phase I trial establishes tumor-selective ALA uptake and a tolerable photodynamic therapy regimen for cutaneous neurofibromas, with apoptosis as a treatment readout.

papers.title: Targeting Sporadic and Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) Related Refractory Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumors (MPNST) in a Phase II Study of Everolimus in Combination with Bevacizumab (SARC016).
papers.summary: In a phase II trial, everolimus plus bevacizumab produced a 12% clinical benefit rate in refractory malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors and did not meet the prespecified activity threshold, despite pharmacodynamic changes in VEGF and VEGFR2. An Nf1/p53-mutant mouse study cited by the paper showed delayed tumor growth with sirolimus, but no tumor shrinkage was observed in the clinical trial.
papers.why: This phase II trial directly evaluates a combination targeting mTOR and angiogenesis in refractory NF1-associated MPNST, although it did not meet its activity target.

papers.title: Novel molecular targeted therapies for patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 with inoperable plexiform neurofibromas: a comprehensive review.
papers.summary: This review reports that MEK inhibitors and cabozantinib reduce plexiform neurofibroma burden and improve pain in selected patients with neurofibromatosis type 1, with selumetinib showing the strongest evidence and receiving regulatory approval for symptomatic inoperable tumors. mTOR inhibition with everolimus or sirolimus did not shrink human tumors, and toxicity, delayed responses, and immature long-term data remain important limitations.
papers.why: Synthesizes clinical and trial evidence for multiple targeted therapies and response outcomes in inoperable NF1 plexiform neurofibromas.

papers.title: Revised diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis type 1 and Legius syndrome: an international consensus recommendation.
papers.summary: This international consensus statement revises clinical and genetic criteria for diagnosing neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), mosaic NF1, Legius syndrome, and mosaic Legius syndrome. It emphasizes early molecular confirmation, careful distinction from phenotypically overlapping RASopathies, and improved interpretation of NF1 pathogenic and mosaic variants.
papers.why: The international consensus directly defines updated clinical and genetic criteria for diagnosing and differentiating NF1.

papers.title: PRC2 is recurrently inactivated through EED or SUZ12 loss in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.
papers.summary: PRC2 is recurrently inactivated through EED or SUZ12 loss in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors, including NF1-associated MPNSTs, causing loss of H3K27me3 and activation of normally repressed developmental regulators. H3K27me3 immunohistochemistry tracked functional PRC2 status, while SUZ12 restoration partially reversed molecular and growth defects in an NF1-associated MPNST cell line.
papers.why: Restoring a missing PRC2 component reduced MPNST cell growth in NF1-associated malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor cells.

papers.title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlation in NF1: Evidence for a More Severe Phenotype Associated with Missense Mutations Affecting NF1 Codons 844-848.
papers.summary: This observational cohort study identifies NF1 missense variants affecting codons 844–848 as a genotype–phenotype risk correlate for severe neurofibromatosis type 1, particularly plexiform and symptomatic spinal neurofibromas, optic pathway gliomas, malignancies, and skeletal abnormalities. It also reports that p.Leu847Pro and p.Gly848 variants may define more specific high-risk subgroups, but molecularly engineered p.Gly848Arg mice did not reproduce the human optic pathway glioma or plexiform neurofibroma phenotype.
papers.why: Establishes an NF1 genotype associated with increased plexiform neurofibroma, spinal neurofibroma, optic pathway glioma, skeletal abnormality, and malignancy risk for clinical counseling.

papers.title: Emerging genotype-phenotype relationships in patients with large NF1 deletions.
papers.summary: This review reports that large NF1 microdeletions are associated with a more severe phenotype than intragenic NF1 mutations, including increased neurofibroma burden, intellectual disability, overgrowth, dysmorphic facial features, cardiovascular anomalies, and increased malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour risk. It identifies SUZ12, RNF135, ATAD5, OMG, and ADAP2 as potential modifiers and highlights whole-body MRI, serial 18Fluorodeoxyglucose PET, standardized clinical assessment, and gene-editing experiments as useful research resources and methods.
papers.why: The review identifies NF1 microdeletion and SUZ12 co-deletion as concrete biomarkers for distinguishing high-risk neurofibroma and MPNST phenotypes within NF1.

papers.title: Midkine activation of CD8+ T cells establishes a neuron-immune-cancer axis responsible for low-grade glioma growth.
papers.summary: The paper establishes a neuron–T cell–microglia axis that supports neurofibromatosis type 1 low-grade glioma growth: NF1-mutant neurons produce midkine, which activates LRP1/calcineurin/NFAT1 signaling in T cells to induce CCL4 and consequent microglial CCL5 production. Disrupting T-cell entry or depletion, MDK signaling, microglial NFκB signaling, or CCL5-dependent survival signaling attenuates tumor proliferation in preclinical models, while high CD8, CCL5, or CD44 expression is associated with poorer survival in human low-grade glioma datasets.
papers.why: This study directly establishes an experimentally testable neuron-immune-cancer mechanism and useful models and biomarkers for NF1-associated low-grade glioma.

papers.title: High Incidence of Noonan Syndrome Features Including Short Stature and Pulmonic Stenosis in Patients carrying NF1 Missense Mutations Affecting p.Arg1809: Genotype-Phenotype Correlation.
papers.summary: The paper identifies a distinct NF1 genotype–phenotype correlation caused by five pathogenic missense variants affecting NF1 p.Arg1809: patients commonly have multiple café-au-lait macules, Noonan-like features, pulmonic stenosis, short stature, and developmental or learning difficulties, but rarely have neurofibromas or symptomatic optic pathway gliomas. Cultured melanocytes from a segmental NF1 lesion provide evidence that p.Arg1809Cys acts as a loss-of-function mutation in melanocytes and contributes to a localized pigmentary phenotype.
papers.why: Defines a recurrent NF1 genotype associated with a mild neurofibromatosis phenotype enriched for short stature, pulmonic stenosis, and developmental or learning difficulties.

papers.title: Neurofibromatosis 1 French national guidelines based on an extensive literature review since 1966.
papers.summary: This French evidence review identifies longitudinal, age-specific surveillance, clinical and genetic diagnostics, imaging, surgery, and selected systemic therapies for neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). It reports promising selumetinib activity in inoperable plexiform neurofibroma and NF-associated optic pathway glioma, but finds insufficient or null benefit for tipifarnib, sirolimus, pirfenidone, imatinib, radiotherapy for benign plexiform tumors, and statins for cognitive impairment.
papers.why: Directly provides a comprehensive clinical management and monitoring framework for NF1, including diagnostic and age-specific care recommendations.

papers.title: Clinical spectrum of individuals with pathogenic NF1 missense variants affecting p.Met1149, p.Arg1276, and p.Lys1423: genotype-phenotype study in neurofibromatosis type 1.
papers.summary: This observational genotype–phenotype study identifies clinically distinct NF1 presentations associated with recurrent p.Met1149, p.Arg1276, and p.Lys1423 missense variants. p.Met1149 is associated with a mild phenotype, whereas p.Arg1276 and p.Lys1423 are associated with Noonan-like features, cardiovascular abnormalities, and distinct neurofibroma patterns that can guide stratification, counseling, surveillance, and management.
papers.why: A cohort of 281 carriers provides variant-specific evidence for Noonan-like phenotypes, cardiovascular abnormalities, spinal neurofibromas, and phenotypic severity that can support NF1 counseling and management stratification.

papers.title: ReNeu: A Pivotal, Phase IIb Trial of Mirdametinib in Adults and Children With Symptomatic Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Associated Plexiform Neurofibroma.
papers.summary: In the single-arm ReNeu phase IIb trial, mirdametinib produced confirmed objective responses, deep and durable reductions in plexiform neurofibroma volume, and clinically meaningful improvements in pain and health-related quality of life in 58 adults and 56 children with symptomatic NF1-associated plexiform neurofibroma. Treatment was generally well tolerated, although dermatitis acneiform, diarrhea, and other adverse events occurred, and the study did not determine off-treatment durability or optimal treatment duration.
papers.why: The pivotal ReNeu trial provides strong same-disease evidence for mirdametinib with confirmed tumor-volume reduction and meaningful pain and quality-of-life improvement.

papers.title: Zebrafish neurofibromatosis type 1 genes have redundant functions in tumorigenesis and embryonic development.
papers.summary: Stable germline loss of both zebrafish NF1 orthologues, nf1a and nf1b, produced an NF1-relevant model with glial and melanophore defects, motor and learning abnormalities, and larval lethality, while one wild-type nf1 allele was sufficient for normal early development. In a p53-mutant background, partial nf1 loss accelerated and increased the penetrance of high-grade gliomas and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors, with variable ERK or mTOR pathway hyperactivation.
papers.why: The study creates and validates multiple zebrafish NF1 models with disease-relevant pigmentation, nervous-system, and tumor phenotypes.

papers.title: Neuronal hyperexcitability drives central and peripheral nervous system tumor progression in models of neurofibromatosis-1.
papers.summary: This paper shows that tumor-associated NF1 mutations cause HCN-regulated hyperexcitability in retinal ganglion cells and dorsal root ganglion neurons, leading to increased secretion of tumor-promoting paracrine factors. Activating HCN channels with lamotrigine reduced midkine or COL1A2 activity and attenuated optic pathway glioma and plexiform neurofibroma progression in mouse models, whereas the NF1 p.Arg1809Cys mutation was associated with preserved neuronal function and absence of these tumors.
papers.why: Mouse experiments demonstrate that neuronal hyperexcitability promotes NF1-associated tumors and that activating HCN channels attenuates activity-regulated paracrine signaling and tumor progression.

papers.title: Comprehensive RNA Analysis of the NF1 Gene in Classically Affected NF1 Affected Individuals Meeting NIH Criteria has High Sensitivity and Mutation Negative Testing is Reassuring in Isolated Cases With Pigmentary Features Only.
papers.summary: Comprehensive blood RNA analysis combined with genomic confirmation detected potentially causative NF1 variants in approximately 96% of 361 individuals meeting classic NIH criteria and was more sensitive than DNA analysis alone. Testing also identified a subset of clinically suspected Legius syndrome caused by SPRED1 variants and revealed an association between dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumour and an absence of identifiable NF1 or SPRED1 variants.
papers.why: Comprehensive RNA testing achieved approximately 96% sensitivity in presumed NF1 cases and provided clinically useful diagnostic risk reduction after a negative result.

papers.title: Genetically engineered minipigs model the major clinical features of human neurofibromatosis type 1.
papers.summary: The paper establishes a genetically engineered NF1R1947*/+ Ossabaw minipig model that reproduces major human neurofibromatosis type 1 features, including café au lait macules, neurofibromas, optic pathway glioma-like lesions, and cell-type-specific loss of heterozygosity. The model also supports pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic testing of targeted therapy, with oral PD0325901 strongly suppressing ERK phosphorylation in peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
papers.why: The engineered minipig reproduces major NF1 manifestations and provides a platform for natural-history studies, imaging, biomarker development, and therapy testing.

papers.title: Human iPSC-Derived Neurons and Cerebral Organoids Establish Differential Effects of Germline NF1 Gene Mutations.
papers.summary: The paper shows that all seven tested heterozygous NF1 mutations increased RAS activity and proliferation in human neural progenitor cells and astrocytes, while neuronal dopamine levels, apoptosis, and neurogenesis showed mutation-specific effects. Isogenic NF1-mutant human iPSC lines, patient-derived lines, cerebral organoids, and engineered Nf1 mice provide complementary platforms for modeling shared and variant-specific CNS abnormalities in neurofibromatosis type 1.
papers.why: This study directly develops multiple NF1 patient-mutation iPSC and cerebral-organoid models and demonstrates mutation-specific cellular phenotypes.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of NF1 and Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Genotype-Phenotype Correlations in a Chinese Population.
papers.summary: Integrated molecular analysis of 109 Chinese patients with NF1-like phenotypes identified pathogenic NF1 variants in 89% of families and 93% of probands meeting NIH criteria. The study supports sequential Sanger sequencing, multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification, and cDNA sequencing as a sensitive diagnostic strategy, particularly for pediatric patients with limited café-au-lait spots, but found no clear mutation-locus–phenotype correlations.
papers.why: The study validates a multi-method genetic testing workflow that detects NF1 variants in 89% of NF1-like probands and supports interpreting patients presenting only with multiple café-au-lait spots.

papers.title: Multiplatform molecular analyses refine classification of gliomas arising in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1.
papers.summary: Multiplatform profiling of 47 gliomas from patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 identified an indolent group characterized mainly by biallelic NF1 inactivation and a distinct DNA methylation signature, and an aggressive group with additional cell-cycle, telomere-maintenance, and other oncogenic alterations. Off-label selumetinib or trametinib produced stable disease or regression in five patients with biallelic NF1 inactivation lacking additional oncogenic alterations, whereas three of four patients with molecular high-grade tumors progressed during single-agent MEK inhibition.
papers.why: Multiplatform profiling and MEK-inhibitor response data define actionable molecular subgroups and show benefit of MEK inhibition in NF1-inactivated gliomas without additional oncogenic alterations.

papers.title: Dual mTORC1/2 inhibition induces anti-proliferative effect in NF1-associated plexiform neurofibroma and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor cells.
papers.summary: The study shows that the dual mTORC1/2 inhibitor AZD8055 suppresses mTOR signaling, protein synthesis, proliferation, migration, anchorage-independent growth, and cell-cycle progression in NF1-associated MPNST cell lines and PNF-derived primary Schwann cells. Combining AZD8055 with the MEK inhibitor PD0325901 or with BET bromodomain inhibitors produces synergistic antiproliferative effects in vitro, but efficacy in rigorous in vivo models and patients remains untested.
papers.why: The study provides experimental drug-response data in NF1-associated plexiform neurofibroma and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor models, including synergistic combinations.

papers.title: Chromosome 8 gain is associated with high-grade transformation in MPNST.
papers.summary: This study establishes and characterizes eight NF1-associated malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) patient-derived xenograft lines, showing that they retain parental tumor histologic, expression, and broad copy-number features while displaying extensive intratumoral and intertumoral heterogeneity. It identifies chromosome 8q gain as a nearly universal, early copy-number event in NF1-MPNST, associates the gain with poorer survival in soft-tissue sarcoma datasets, and nominates HEY1, MYC, and RAD21 as genes on the gained region requiring further functional study.
papers.why: The paper develops an NF1-MPNST patient-derived xenograft platform and validates chromosome 8 gain as a recurrent genomic biomarker associated with malignant transformation and poor outcome.

papers.title: Patient-derived iPSC-cerebral organoid modeling of the 17q11.2 microdeletion syndrome establishes CRLF3 as a critical regulator of neurogenesis.
papers.summary: The study shows that the 1.4-Mb 17q11.2 NF1-total gene deletion (NF1-TGD) causes increased neural stem-cell proliferation through RAS hyperactivation, while reduced CRLF3 expression causes defective neuronal differentiation, survival, maturation, and dendritic development through impaired RhoA signaling. Pharmacologic activation of RhoA with CN03 rescued these neuronal defects in patient-derived cerebral organoids, and CRLF3 c.1166T>C (p.Leu389Pro) was associated with higher autistic trait burden in a small NF1 cohort.
papers.why: This study develops a patient-derived NF1 total-gene-deletion cerebral organoid model and experimentally identifies CRLF3-dependent neurogenesis defects.

papers.title: Use of bevacizumab as a single agent or in adjunct with traditional chemotherapy regimens in children with unresectable or progressive low-grade glioma.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 15 children with progressive pediatric low-grade glioma, two of whom had neurofibromatosis type 1, bevacizumab-based therapy was associated with rapid radiological and clinical improvement, including improved vision in some NF1 patients. Toxicity was generally manageable, although severe hypertension and proteinura required interruption in some patients, and disease control was often not durable after treatment cessation.
papers.why: The report includes NF1-associated pediatric low-grade glioma and shows rapid tumor control and visual or functional improvement in treated patients.

papers.title: The Role of [18F]FDG-PET/CT in Predicting Malignant Transformation of Plexiform Neurofibromas in Neurofibromatosis-1.
papers.summary: This systematic review finds that FDG-PET/CT is a useful noninvasive diagnostic test for identifying malignant transformation of plexiform neurofibromas to MPNST in adults and children with neurofibromatosis type 1, with generally high sensitivity and negative predictive value. However, overlapping SUVmax values, no validated universal cutoff, technical variability, and limited evidence prevent FDG-PET/CT from replacing histopathology or clinical assessment.
papers.why: Systematic review and validation evidence support FDG-PET/CT and SUVmax measurement as a noninvasive approach for identifying malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors in NF1.

papers.title: Performance Evaluation of SpliceAI for the Prediction of Splicing of NF1 Variants.
papers.summary: In 285 NF1 variants from 653 patients, SpliceAI predicted experimentally confirmed splicing alterations with 94.5% sensitivity and 94.3% specificity at a Δ Score cutoff above 0.22, outperforming the combined MaxEntScan/splice Site Finder-like analysis. Complementary DNA and genomic DNA sequencing provided the functional confirmation and remains central to the laboratory workflow, while the authors note that gene- and variant-specific cutoff validation is needed.
papers.why: The study validates SpliceAI for predicting splice-altering NF1 variants and provides a laboratory-usable threshold for variant interpretation.

papers.title: Optic Pathway Glioma in Type 1 Neurofibromatosis: Review of Its Pathogenesis, Diagnostic Assessment, and Treatment Recommendations.
papers.summary: This review reports that optic pathway glioma occurs in approximately 15–20% of children with neurofibromatosis type 1 but is usually indolent and only one-third requires treatment. It identifies MRI, serial visual-acuity testing, and optical coherence tomography of the retinal nerve fiber layer as useful diagnostic or monitoring approaches, while showing that chemotherapy and MEK inhibition can control disease but do not consistently restore vision and have important limitations.
papers.why: This review consolidates diagnostic workflows, outcome monitoring, genetically engineered models, and treatment strategies specifically for NF1-associated optic pathway glioma.

papers.title: Motor learning in children with neurofibromatosis type I.
papers.summary: In a comparison of 70 children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and 19 age-matched controls, children with NF1 had lower visual-motor integration and fine motor performance scores. Prism-induced hand-movement adaptation was mildly reduced, whereas baseline saccadic performance, saccadic adaptation, and goal-directed hand-movement performance did not differ from controls; the findings do not support a general cerebellar dysfunction as the sole cause of NF1-associated motor problems.
papers.why: The paper directly tests quantitative motor-performance and motor-learning endpoints in 70 children with NF1 and provides data on their utility and limitations for capturing NF1 motor dysfunction.

papers.title: Pharmacological and genomic profiling of neurofibromatosis type 1 plexiform neurofibroma-derived schwann cells.
papers.summary: The paper establishes a genomic and pharmacological resource based on primary and immortalized Schwann cell lines derived from human neurofibromatosis type 1 plexiform neurofibromas, including NF1−/−, NF1+/−, and NF1+/+ genotypes. It validates a 1536-well dose-response cell-proliferation platform and demonstrates that the immortalized lines are suitable for screening oncology compounds and studying NF1-associated plexiform neurofibroma biology.
papers.why: The paper directly develops and characterizes NF1 plexiform-neurofibroma Schwann cell resources, genomic profiles, and a reusable compound-screening assay.

papers.title: The RASopathies: from pathogenetics to therapeutics.
papers.summary: This review identifies neurofibromatosis type 1 as a RAS/MAPK-pathway disorder and reports selumetinib as the first FDA-approved RASopathy treatment, specifically for pediatric NF1 patients with symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas. It highlights Legius syndrome as a mechanistically related RASopathy and shows that MEK inhibition can correct only selected phenotypes in SPRED1-deficient models, illustrating genotype- and outcome-dependent transfer of RAS/MAPK therapies.
papers.why: Directly reviews RAS/MAPK-targeted therapeutics and models across RASopathies including NF1, making the approaches especially relevant for reuse.

papers.title: Clinical and Genetic Findings in Children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1, Legius Syndrome, and Other Related Neurocutaneous Disorders.
papers.summary: In 281 mostly pediatric patients evaluated for neurofibromatosis type 1, Legius syndrome, and other neurocutaneous disorders, a combined molecular strategy using targeted next generation sequencing, RNA analysis, and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification achieved a molecular diagnosis in 85.1% of cases. The approach was most successful in clinically diagnosed NF1, while isolated café au lait macules, mosaic disease, and other overlapping disorders remained less frequently resolved and yielded occasional uncertain variants requiring functional interpretation.
papers.why: The study validates a combined sequencing, MLPA, and RNA-analysis workflow for molecular diagnosis of NF1 and phenotypically overlapping neurocutaneous disorders.

papers.title: Physical, cognitive, and psychosocial predictors of functional disability and health-related quality of life in adolescents with neurofibromatosis-1.
papers.summary: In an observational study of adolescents with neurofibromatosis type 1, worse emotional functioning was associated with lower health-related quality of life, whereas more days of pain was associated with greater self-reported functional disability. Disease severity was associated with cognitive functioning but not with pain, quality of life, functional disability, or emotional functioning, and the parent-reported functional-disability regression model was not significant.
papers.why: The NF1 cohort identifies measurable cognitive, pain, emotional, functional-disability, and quality-of-life outcomes that can be used in research and clinical studies.

papers.title: Examination of the genetic factors underlying the cognitive variability associated with neurofibromatosis type 1.
papers.summary: In 497 children with genetically confirmed neurofibromatosis type 1, cognitive ability was shifted downward relative to the general population, while variability and familial correlation among individuals with intragenic NF1 variants resembled that of the general population. The only significant genotype–phenotype association identified was lower full-scale, verbal, and performance IQ in children carrying an NF1 chromosomal microdeletion, supporting additional genetic evaluation for markedly low IQ in children with intragenic NF1 variants.
papers.why: A large genetically confirmed NF1 cohort links chromosomal microdeletions to lower IQ and proposes IQ-based triage for additional cognitive evaluation.

papers.title: A nationwide evaluation of bevacizumab-based treatments in pediatric low-grade glioma in the UK: Safety, efficacy, visual morbidity, and outcomes.
papers.summary: This nationwide UK service evaluation found that bevacizumab-based treatment provided short-term radiological disease control and visual stabilization in children with pediatric low-grade glioma, with particularly favorable radiological and visual outcomes in children with NF1-associated optic pathway glioma. Most patients had pre-existing visual morbidity, and visual deterioration remained common in the worst-affected eyes, while treatment toxicity was generally limited.
papers.why: The nationwide cohort directly reports real-world bevacizumab-based treatment outcomes in pediatric low-grade glioma, including a superior sustained visual outcome for NF1-associated optic pathway glioma.

papers.title: Subependymal giant cell astrocytoma-like astrocytoma: a neoplasm with a distinct phenotype and frequent neurofibromatosis type-1-association.
papers.summary: This study identifies subependymal giant cell astrocytoma-like astrocytoma as a morphologically and molecularly distinct tumor occurring frequently in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). NF1 inactivation was found in all sequenced cases, while alternative lengthening of telomeres occurred in a subset, usually without ATRX or DAXX alterations, suggesting additional DNA-maintenance mechanisms that require functional validation.
papers.why: Reports molecular and diagnostic characterization of astrocytomas occurring in NF1, identifying recurrent NF1 inactivation and a distinct NF1-associated tumor phenotype.

papers.title: Reproducibility of cognitive endpoints in clinical trials: lessons from neurofibromatosis type 1.
papers.summary: Reanalysis of the STARS phase II trial shows that many individual cognitive and behavioral endpoints had poor test-retest reliability in children with neurofibromatosis type 1, whereas confirmatory factor analysis produced latent domains with generally acceptable reproducibility. Lovastatin showed small, consistent, nonsignificant cognitive effects and no clinical benefit, while the paper recommends piloting endpoints and using theory-based data reduction in future neurofibromatosis type 1 cognitive trials.
papers.why: Develops and validates reproducible cognitive endpoints and data-reduction methods for clinical trials in children with NF1.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of NF1 and non-NF1 congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia based on germline NF1 variants: genetic and clinical analysis of 75 patients.
papers.summary: In a cohort of 75 patients with congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia, germline pathogenic NF1 variants distinguished clinically defined NF1-associated CPT from non-NF1 CPT, being found in 80.0% of NF1 cases and none of 20 non-NF1 cases. Despite generally similar tibial and pathological features, non-NF1 CPT was more frequently associated with cystic lesions and brace use, while NF1-associated CPT showed heterogeneous pseudarthrosis phenotypes without a direct variant-level genotype–phenotype relationship.
papers.why: The study provides a validated genetic-testing approach and genotype–phenotype data for distinguishing NF1-associated from non-NF1 congenital tibial pseudarthrosis.

papers.title: Fifty-four novel mutations in the NF1 gene and integrated analyses of the mutations that modulate splicing.
papers.summary: A retrospective series of 378 people referred for NF1 testing identified 127 NF1 variants, including 54 novel variants, and showed that exonic and non-consensus intronic variants can alter NF1 pre-mRNA splicing. Genomic, transcriptomic, and computational analyses characterized aberrant splice sites and splicing-regulatory elements, including post-transcriptional mosaicism caused by c.3362A>G.
papers.why: The combined DNA, RNA, and computational analysis shows that many NF1 variants alter splicing and provides a directly transferable approach for molecular interpretation and diagnostic testing.

papers.title: Feasibility of using NF1-GRD and AAV for gene replacement therapy in NF1-associated tumors.
papers.summary: The study shows that NF1-GRD delivered by lentiviral or AAV vectors suppresses Ras signaling and growth in patient-derived NF1-associated malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor cell lines, with membrane-targeted GRD-C10 being substantially more potent. AAV-DJ efficiently transduced these cells and primary human Schwann cells, but GRD-C10 did not significantly affect NF1-intact sporadic MPNST cells or normal Schwann cells, indicating NF1-dependent specificity and a need for improved in vivo delivery.
papers.why: The study demonstrates that selected AAV vectors deliver a membrane-targeted neurofibromin GRD construct that suppresses Ras signaling and inhibits NF1-associated MPNST cells.

papers.title: Deep genomic analysis of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor cell lines challenges current malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor diagnosis.
papers.summary: This paper shows that commonly used malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) cell lines differ substantially in genomic identity, and that NF1-related cell lines better recapitulate primary NF1-associated MPNST copy-number profiles than sporadic lines. The study identifies misidentified or misdiagnosed cell lines, provides genomic, methylome-based, and cell-identity-marker approaches for differential diagnosis, and reports differential cell-viability responses to selumetinib and JQ1.
papers.why: The study supplies and validates a resource of NF1-related MPNST cell lines and genomic/methylation classifiers for translational research and tumor diagnosis.

papers.title: Sporadic and Familial Variants in NF1: An Explanation of the Wide Variability in Neurocognitive Phenotype?
papers.summary: In an observational study of 96 children with neurofibromatosis type 1, familial cases had lower IQ scores than sporadic cases, while most other cognitive and psychosocial measures did not differ; lower maternal education and family socioeconomic status were associated with the IQ difference. The findings support early, repeated neuropsychological monitoring of affected children but do not identify a disease-modifying treatment or establish a single cause of NF1 phenotypic variability.
papers.why: Evaluates a detailed cognitive profiling battery in children with NF1 and identifies practical contributors to measured neurocognitive heterogeneity.

papers.title: Safety and efficacy of selumetinib in pediatric and adult patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 and plexiform neurofibroma.
papers.summary: In a single-arm phase II trial of 90 Korean pediatric and adult patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 and inoperable plexiform neurofibroma, selumetinib reduced target-tumor volume and improved neurocognitive scores, prepubertal growth, café-au-lait spot intensity, pain, and quality of life. Adverse events were grade 1 or 2, but the lack of a control group, treatment-related malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor in one child, and other design limitations constrain causal and generalizability conclusions.
papers.why: A phase II trial directly demonstrates selumetinib efficacy in pediatric and adult NF1 patients with plexiform neurofibroma.

papers.title: Reprogramming Captures the Genetic and Tumorigenic Properties of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Plexiform Neurofibromas.
papers.summary: The paper reports generation and banking of NF1(−/−) and NF1(+/−) induced pluripotent stem cell lines directly from patient-derived plexiform neurofibroma cells. NF1(−/−) iPSC-derived Schwann cells retained the tumor-associated genomic state, exhibited continuous high proliferation, poor myelination, and formed marker-consistent spheres, providing a non-perishable in vitro model for plexiform neurofibroma research and therapeutic testing.
papers.why: The authors generated and banked NF1-null iPSC lines that reproduce the genomic, proliferative, myelination, and 3D sphere phenotypes of plexiform neurofibroma-derived Schwann cells.

papers.title: Identification of Mutation Regions on NF1 Responsible for High- and Low-Risk Development of Optic Pathway Glioma in Neurofibromatosis Type I.
papers.summary: In a case-control study of 215 patients with neurofibromatosis type I, mutations in the NF1 cysteine/serine-rich domain were associated with higher optic pathway glioma risk, whereas mutations in the HEAT-like repeat region were associated with lower risk. Mutation clustering in the 5′ tertile and mutation type within these domains did not significantly explain optic pathway glioma risk, although the study noted methodological and population limitations.
papers.why: Identifies NF1 mutation regions associated with higher or lower optic-pathway-glioma risk, providing a disease-specific prognostic biomarker.

papers.title: Destabilizing NF1 variants act in a dominant negative manner through neurofibromin dimerization.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The study shows that destabilizing NF1 missense variants, especially at codons 844–848, reduce mutant neurofibromin expression and act in a dominant-negative manner by heterodimerizing with and destabilizing wild-type neurofibromin. A cryo-EM structure, biochemical experiments, and disease-relevant Schwann cells support a protein-stability mechanism that increases RAS signaling and provides a structure-guided strategy for predicting and suppressing destabilizing variants.
papers.why: Directly develops and validates structural and functional approaches for predicting destabilizing dominant-negative NF1 variants.

papers.title: 126 novel mutations in Italian patients with neurofibromatosis type 1.
papers.summary: In 513 unrelated Italian patients with suspected or clinically defined neurofibromatosis type 1, the study identified 225 pathogenic NF1 variants, including 126 novel variants, and found pathogenic mutations in 36 of 159 patients who did not meet NIH clinical criteria. Integrating DNA and RNA analyses increased mutation detection to 87%; type 1 microdeletions were associated with a higher frequency of intellectual disability, but no new significant genotype–phenotype correlations were identified.
papers.why: Reports validated molecular testing workflows, a large mutation dataset, and improved detection of NF1 variants in clinically inconclusive cases.

papers.title: AZD6244 Hydrogen Sulfate for Children With Nervous System Tumors
papers.summary:

\- Plexiform neurofibromas are tumors that grow in and around nerves. The only way to treat them is with surgery. Some of these tumors cannot be completely removed. The tumors may be too large, too numerous, or in a bad location for surgery. An experimental drug called AZD6244 hydrogen sulfate may be able to prevent the tumors from growing, slow down their growth, or shrink them. This drug has been tested in adults with cancer and in children with some types of brain cancer. This study will test how well this drug works with these types of tumors.

papers.title: Early Phase Study Evaluating MEK and MDM2 Inhibition in Patients With NF1 and MPNST
papers.summary: This is a phase 0/1/2, multi-site study to evaluate the MEK inhibitor Selumetinib with the MDM2 Inhibitor APG-115 in patients with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and pre-malignant and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors

papers.title: Innovation in the Treatment of Persistent Pain in Adults With NF1: Implementation of the iCanCope Mobile Application- Clinical Trial
papers.summary: To demonstrate the initial feasibility and determine preliminary impact on clinical outcomes of the iCanCope-NF program in a pilot RCT. If successful this pilot study will support conducting a larger randomized control trial (RCT). The primary research question is what is the feasibility of the iCanCope-NF program? The investigators define feasibility as (1) rates of accrual and dropout, daily log-ins, engagement, and outcome measures completed and (2) perceptions regarding intervention acceptability and satisfaction; and what are the levels of engagement. log-ins, with the intervention? papers.title: A Phase 2, Open-Label Study to Evaluate the Safety and Effects of HLX-1502 in Patients With Neurofibromatosis Type 1
papers.summary: The trial will be an open label, single arm, phase 2 study to assess the tolerability and efficacy of HLX-1502 in participants with NF1 that are 16 years or older in age with progressive and/or symptomatic PN. This study will also investigate the safety and efficacy of HLX-1502 in a small cohort of 12 to 15 year olds.

papers.title: Selumetinib Paediatric NF1 Japan Study
papers.summary: This is a phase I open label study designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, PK and efficacy of selumetinib in Japanese paediatric patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 and inoperable and symptomatic plexiform neurofibroma.

papers.title: A Study of the Drugs Selumetinib Versus Carboplatin/Vincristine in Patients With Neurofibromatosis and Low-Grade Glioma
papers.summary: This phase III trial studies if selumetinib works just as well as the standard treatment with carboplatin/vincristine (CV) for subjects with NF1-associated low grade glioma (LGG), and to see if selumetinib is better than CV in improving vision in subjects with LGG of the optic pathway (vision nerves). Selumetinib is a drug that works by blocking some enzymes that low-grade glioma tumor cells need for their growth. This results in killing tumor cells. papers.summary:

papers.title: Fludeoxyglucose F 18 Positron Emission Tomography and Magnetic Resonance Perfusion Imaging in Patients With Neurofibromatosis 1 and Plexiform Neurofibroma
papers.summary:
RATIONALE: New imaging procedures such as fludeoxyglucose F 18 positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and magnetic resonance (MR) perfusion imaging may improve the ability to detect disease progression, help doctors predict a patient's response to treatment, and help plan the most effective treatment.

PURPOSE: This diagnostic trial is studying how well FDG-PET and MR perfusion imaging work in finding disease progression and determining response to treatment in patients with neurofibromatosis 1 and plexiform neurofibroma.

papers.title: Phase II Trial of Sunitinib (SU011248) in Patients With Recurrent or Inoperable Meningioma
papers.summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out what effects, good and/or bad, sunitinib has on patients and their tumors. At this time, no drugs are routinely used to treat meningioma, hemangioblastoma or hemangiopericytoma. Only surgery and radiation therapy are known to be useful.

Sunitinib is a drug approved for advanced kidney cancer. Sunitinib is also being studied for other tumors. It may be useful in the treatment of brain tumors because it can prevent formation of new blood vessels that allow tumor cells to survive and grow.

papers.title: Interventions for Reading Disabilities in NF1
papers.summary: Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) is a common genetic disorder that is associated with a four times greater risk of learning disabilities, including reading disabilities, and a deficiency of neurofibromin - a protein important in a signaling pathway that regulates learning and memory. Our previous work (NS49096) demonstrated that school-age children with NF+RD can respond to standard phonologically-based reading tutoring originally developed to treat reading disability in the general population. papers.title: A Study to Evaluate the Feasibility of a Physiologic Biomarker to Assess Pain and Other Sensory Problems Using Pupillometry in Participants With Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1)
papers.summary:
Background:

Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a genetic condition that causes tumors to grow along the nerves in the skin, brain, and other parts of the body. People with NF1 often have pain and may experience other abnormal sensations like itching, numbness, or tingling. These symptoms can affect their daily life. Researchers want to learn more about these symptoms and find better ways to measure pain in people with NF1.

Objective:

To learn if a device called the AlgometRx Nociometer(Registered trademark) is effective in measuring pain or other abnormal sensations in people with NF1.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Selumetinib in Adults With NF1 Who Have Symptomatic, Inoperable Plexiform Neurofibromas
papers.summary: A global study to demonstrate the effectiveness of selumetinib in participants with NF1 who have symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas.

papers.title: Low-dose Selumetinib for the Treatment of Plexiform Neurofibromas in Chinese Children
papers.summary: The goal of this study is to compare the efficacy and safety of low-dose and internationally recommended standard dose of selumetinib in the treatment of plexiform neurofibromas in Chinese children.

papers.title: Pomalidomide in Treating Younger Patients With Recurrent, Progressive, or Refractory Central Nervous System Tumors
papers.summary: This phase I trial studies the side effects and best dose of pomalidomide in treating younger patients with tumors of the brain or spine (central nervous system) that have come back or are continuing to grow. Pomalidomide may interfere with the ability of tumor cells to grow and spread and may also stimulate the immune system to kill tumor cells.

papers.title: Topical Imiquimod 5% Cream for Treatment of Cutaneous Neurofibromas in Adults With Neurofibromatosis 1
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine if imiquimod cream can reverse the growth of neurofibromas. Imiquimod is a skin cream that works by stimulating the body's immune system to respond to tumors. Imiquimod cream is approved for use in patients with various skin lesions, including actinic keratosis, superficial basal cell carcinoma, and external genital warts. Information from these studies, as well as previous laboratory studies, suggest that imiquimod cream may help shrink neurofibromas or keep them from growing.

papers.title: Efficacy of Skin Cooling in Reducing Pain Associated With Non-invasive Treatments of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Cutaneous Neurofibromas
papers.summary: This study will evaluate the effectiveness of skin cooling in increasing tolerability of four treatments in Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Cutaneous Neurofibromas. These treatments are: a 980nm laser, a 755nm laser, radio-frequency injection, and a Kybella injection. Each patient will have a treatment and a control site..

papers.title: Assessing the Efficacy of Repeat, Monthly Treatments of Alexandrite Laser for NF1-associated Cutaneous Neurofibromas (cNFs)
papers.summary:

Will performing up to 6 months of treatment sessions with alexandrite laser will result in tolerable local skin reactions and reduction in both individual cNF size by \>50% as well as improved cNF appearance in the treated field? papers.title: From Molecules to Cognition: Inhibitory Mechanisms in ASD and NF1
papers.summary:
This study aims to investigate synaptic physiology and behavioral inhibition in patients with NF1 and ASD and to answer whether inhibitory deficits at these levels are modulated by lovastatin.

papers.title: Functional Imaging and Reading Deficit in Children With NF1
papers.summary: A monocenter pilot study on the acceptability and feasibility of a functional MRI protocol in children with NF1 with or without reading disabilities.

papers.title: Pharmacokinetics, Safety and Efficacy of the Selumetinib Granule Formulation in Children Aged ≥1 to <7 Years With NF1-related Symptomatic, Inoperable PN
papers.summary: This study is designed to define a dosing regimen and assess the pharmacokinetics(PK) and safety of the granule formulation; the study will also include descriptive analyses of exploratory efficacy endpoints. The study will inform the benefit risk profile of the granule formulation in children aged ≥ 1 to \< 7 years with NF1 related symptomatic, inoperable PN.

papers.title: Vaccine Therapy in Treating Patients with Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor That is Recurrent or Cannot Be Removed by Surgery
papers.summary: This phase I trial studies the side effects and the best dose of a vaccine therapy in treating patients with malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor that cannot be removed by surgery (unresectable) or has come back after a period of improvement (recurrent). Vaccines made from a gene-modified virus may kill tumor cells expressing a gene called neurofibromin 1 (NF1) without affecting surrounding normal cells and may also help the body build an effective immune response to kill tumor cells.

papers.title: Feasibility and Tolerability of IMLYGIC for the Treatment of Cutaneous Neurofibromas in Adults With NF1
papers.summary: This study is designed to establish the foundation for a new therapy for neurofibromatosis Type I (NF1)-related cutaneous neurofibromas (cNFs) by assessing the feasibility and efficacy of IMLYGIC in adults with NF1 and cNFs who desire local treatment of their cNF due to disfigurement, progression, pain, itching or other concerns. This is a single institutional Phase 1 study with a safety run-in to assess the feasibility and efficacy of IMLYGIC monotherapy in NF1 patients with cNFs. This result will be transferred to patients with Noonan Syndrome. lamotrigine is most likely a more effective and promising substance improving synaptic plasticity and consecutive cognitive function. papers.summary:

Secondary Aims:

To evaluate the effect of Lovastatin ™ on measures of executive function, behavior and quality of life in children with NF1 and cognitive deficits.

papers.title: Tolerability of Device Based Therapies for Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Cutaneous Neurofibromas
papers.summary: This study will evaluate the tolerability and effectiveness of three FDA-approved treatments in Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Cutaneous Neurofibromas. These treatments are: a 1064nm laser, a 755nm laser, and a Kybella injection. Each patient will have a treatment and a control site.

papers.title: Selumetinib for the Prevention of Plexiform Neurofibroma Growth in NF Type 1
papers.summary: Plexiform neurofibromas (PN) are known to cause significant morbidity in children with NF1. The recent FDA approval for selumetinib in children 2 years and older with inoperable symptomatic PN was based on the finding that selumetinib shrinks the majority of PN in children with NF1 and results in clinically meaningful benefit such as improvement in pain or range of motion. papers.title: Vinblastine and Carboplatin in Treating Young Patients With Newly Diagnosed or Recurrent Low-Grade Glioma
papers.summary:
RATIONALE: Drugs used in chemotherapy, such as vinblastine and carboplatin, work in different ways to stop the growth of tumor cells, either by killing the cells or by stopping them from dividing. Giving more than one drug (combination chemotherapy) may kill more tumor cells.

PURPOSE: This phase I trial is studying the side effects and best dose of vinblastine when given together with carboplatin in treating young patients with newly diagnosed or recurrent low-grade glioma.

papers.title: PF-07284892 in Participants With Advanced Solid Tumors
papers.summary: The purpose of this first-in-patient, open label study is to determine the maximum tolerated dose and/or recommended dose for further study of PF-07284892 as a single agent and in combination with lorlatinib, encorafenib and cetuximab, or binimetinib and evaluate the pharmacokinetics, safety, and preliminary clinical activity of single agent and each combination therapy.

papers.title: Antioxidant Therapy With N-acetylcysteine for Children With Neurofibromatosis Type 1
papers.summary: Children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) commonly suffer from the effects of cognitive, behavioral, and motor impairments. At present, there is no specific treatment for this NF1 complication. In this project, the investigators will assess the safety and clinical benefit of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) as a pharmacological intervention in children with NF1. This drug choice is based on the recent findings from mouse models to study the central nervous system manifestations of NF1 at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center (CCHMC). papers.title: Feasibility and Clinically Application of Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting
papers.summary: This study will look at the feasibility of using magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) in children, adolescents and young adults (AYA) with and without brain tumors. This study will also look at subjects with and without neurofibromatosis type 1(NF1), a genetic disorder that affects the growth of nervous system cells. papers.title: Trial of Selumetinib and Bromodomain Inhibitor With Durvalumab for Sarcomas
papers.summary: A multi-institutional open-label phase 1/2 trial of selumetinib in combination with ZEN-3694 and durvalumab in refractory/unresectable sarcomas including MPNST. The phase 1 portion will be separated in two parts and will be open to all patients with refractory/relapsed sarcomas. The phase 2 portion will be for patients with refractory/unresectable NF1-associated MPNST.

papers.title: Efficacy of Mirdametinib Alone or Combination With Radiotherapy for Germline and Sporadic NF1-Altered High-Grade Glioma
papers.summary: This is a phase 2, open label, parallel multi-arm study of mirdametinib in combination with radiation in participants with recurrent sporadic glioblastoma (GBM) harboring NF1 alterations (Cohort 1); participants with NF1 with a newly diagnosed GBM (Cohort 2); mirdametinib alone in other NF1-associated High-Grade Gliomas (Cohort 3).

papers.title: Selumetinib in Treating Young Patients With Recurrent or Refractory Low Grade Glioma
papers.summary: This phase I/II trial studies the side effects and the best dose of selumetinib and how well it works in treating or re-treating young patients with low grade glioma that has come back (recurrent) or does not respond to treatment (refractory). Selumetinib may stop the growth of tumor cells by blocking some of the enzymes needed for cell growth.

papers.title: Combination of Avutometinib and Defactinib for Treatment of Relapsed, Refractory, Metastatic, or Unresectable Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to learn whether the study drugs avutometinib and defactinib can help stop or shrink malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST) that have returned or cannot be removed with surgery.

papers.title: Treatment of NF1-related Plexiform Neurofibroma With Trametinib
papers.summary:
This trial, Treatment of NF1-related plexiform neurofibroma with trametinib; a single arm,open-label study with the goals of volumetric partial remission and pain relief (EudraCT 2018-001846-32, Sponsor protocol number BUS2018-1, related Novartis reference number CTMT212ASE01T) is a pediatric clinical trial that investigates the potential use of the drug trametinib (Mekinist®) as treatment for symptomatic or likely to become symptomatic NF1-related plexiform neurofibromas (PN) in children between 1 year and 17 year and 11 months of age.

papers.title: Trial to Evaluate the Safety of Lovastatin in Individuals With Neurofibromatosis Type I (NF1)
papers.summary: Neurofibromatosis type I (NF1) is a genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 3500 individuals. Half of people with NF1 inherit the condition from a parent, and half have a new occurrence of the condition. The manifestation of NF1 is highly variable and multiple organ systems are typically affected. Some of the more common symptoms include benign neurofibromas, café au lait spots, Lisch nodules (tan spots on the iris of the eye). Some individuals with NF1 also exhibit more severe associated conditions, such as optic pathway tumors (gliomas) or bones bending or curving. Neurocognitive de

papers.title: Selumetinib in Treating Patients With Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and Cutaneous Neurofibroma
papers.summary: This pilot phase II trial studies how well selumetinib works in treating patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 and cutaneous neurofibromas. Selumetinib may stop the growth of tumor cells by blocking some of the enzymes needed for cell growth.

papers.title: Combination Chemotherapy in Treating Patients With Neurofibromatosis and Progressive Plexiform Neurofibromas
papers.summary:
RATIONALE: Drugs used in chemotherapy use different ways to stop tumor cells from dividing so they stop growing or die. Combining methotrexate with vinblastine may be effective treatment for neurofibromatosis type 1 associated with progressive plexiform neurofibromas.

PURPOSE: Phase II trial to study the effectiveness of combination chemotherapy in treating patients who have neurofibromatosis type 1 associated with progressive plexiform neurofibromas.

papers.summary:

Radiation therapy uses high-energy x-rays to kill tumor cells. Giving combination chemotherapy with or without radiation therapy before surgery may make the tumor smaller and reduce the amount of normal tissue that needs to be removed. Giving combination chemotherapy after surgery may kill any tumor cells that remain after surgery.

papers.title: Dosing and Tolerability of Deoxycholic Acid vs. Polidocanol in the Treatment of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Cutaneous Neurofibromas
papers.summary: This study will evaluate the tolerability and effectiveness of two treatments in Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Cutaneous Neurofibromas. These treatments are: Kybella and Asclera injection. Each patient will have a treatment and a control site.

papers.title: A Study of Selumetinib in Chinese Paediatric and Adult Subjects With Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) and Inoperable Plexiform Neurofibromas (PN)
papers.summary: A Phase 1 Open Label Study to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Clinical Efficacy of Selumetinib, a Selective Mitogen Activated Protein Kinase Kinase (MEK) 1 Inhibitor, in Chinese Paediatric and Adult Subjects with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) and Inoperable Plexiform Neurofibromas (PN).

papers.title: Pirfenidone in Treating Young Patients With Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and Plexiform Neurofibromas
papers.summary:
RATIONALE: Chemoprevention therapy is the use of certain drugs to try to prevent the development or recurrence of cancer. Pirfenidone may slow the growth or prevent further development of plexiform neurofibromas.

PURPOSE: Phase I trial to study the effectiveness of pirfenidone in treating young patients who have neurofibromatosis type 1 and plexiform neurofibroma.

papers.title: Mirdametinib Monotherapy in Adults With Neurofibromatosis 1 (NF1) and Cutaneous Neurofibromas (cNF).
papers.summary:
This is a Phase 1/2a, open-label, non-randomized, multi-dose study of mirdametinib monotherapy in adults with NF1 and cNF.

In both Phases of the study, participation in the study will comprise three periods: screening, treatment and post-study safety follow-up to be performed at the NF1 and cNF specialty center: Johns Hopkins University.

papers.title: Evaluation of Percutaneous Cryotherapy in the Treatment of Plexiform Neurofibromas and Unresectable Neurofibromas in Neurofibromatosis Type 1
papers.summary:
Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is an autosomal dominant disease affecting chromosome 17. It is manifested by a neurogenic tumor proliferation that forms cutaneous, subcutaneous or deep neurofibromas.

Neurofibromas can cause functional discomfort, neurogenic pain that is difficult to treat, and severe cosmetic disorders.

Treatment is essentially surgical. It is sometimes a heavy invasive surgery with complicated postoperative follow-up and significant scarring on the aesthetic level. Currently, no systemic treatment has proven its effectiveness in this pathology.

papers.title: Trametinib in Patients With Advanced Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1)-Mutant Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
papers.summary: Phase II trial to evaluate trametinib in patients with locally advanced non-squamous, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors harbor a non-synonymous NF-1 mutation, with progressive disease on at least one prior line of therapy.
