papers.title: A Study of Mirdametinib in Infants and Toddlers With Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Associated Plexiform Neurofibromas
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine the safety, pharmacokinetic (PK), and tolerability of multiple treatment cycles of oral mirdametinib in infants and toddlers (0 to less than \[\<\] 24 months of age) with measurable neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) associated plexiform neurofibromas (PNs) that is symptomatic or asymptomatic but in a high-risk location with a high risk of morbidity.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for neurofibromatosis type 1
suz12 inactivation in p53- and nf1-deficient zebrafish accelerates the onset of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors and expands the spectrum of tumor types.
papers.summary: In a p53/nf1-deficient zebrafish model, CRISPR-Cas9 inactivation of one to three suz12 alleles reduced H3K27me3, increased Ras-Mapk signaling, accelerated MPNST onset and penetrance, and expanded the tumor spectrum. The MEK inhibitor PD-0325901 reduced MPNST growth in transplanted embryos, with SUZ12-mutant NF1-deficient tumors showing greater sensitivity than SUZ12-wild-type controls.

papers.title: Targeting HNRNPU to overcome cisplatin resistance in bladder cancer.
papers.summary: Genome-wide CRISPR screening identified HNRNPU depletion as a strategy that increases cisplatin sensitivity in cisplatin-resistant T24 bladder urothelial carcinoma cells, with supporting xenograft evidence. HNRNPU knockout increased NF1 expression, while NF1 knockdown reversed the improvements in cisplatin sensitivity, proliferation, migration, cell-cycle arrest, and apoptosis, supporting an HNRNPU–NF1 regulatory mechanism.

papers.title: Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screening in hepatocellular carcinoma with lenvatinib resistance.
papers.summary: Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 screening and validation experiments show that NF1 loss drives lenvatinib resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma by reactivating PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK signaling. The MEK inhibitor trametinib suppressed proliferation and tumor growth in NF1-deficient models, identifying a pathway-based strategy that may act downstream of NF1 loss.

papers.title: Genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screens reveal shared and cell-specific mechanisms of resistance to SHP2 inhibition.
papers.summary: Genome-wide and focused CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screens identified NF1 deletion as a recurrent mechanism of resistance to SHP2 inhibition, conferring SHP099 resistance in 12 of 14 cancer cell lines. NF1 is described as a negative regulator of the RAS/ERK pathway, but its specific signaling effect and the therapeutic relevance of this resistance mechanism were not characterized further in NF1-deficient models.

papers.title: Defining CDK12 as a tumor suppressor and therapeutic target in mouse models of tubo-ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: This paper establishes CDK12 as a tumor suppressor and therapeutic vulnerability in tubo-ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC). In engineered mouse and human ovarian cancer systems that also carry Nf1 loss, Cdk12 inactivation accelerates tumorigenesis, increases DNA damage and immune infiltration, and creates a synthetic-lethal dependency on CDK13 that is targeted by the CDK12/13 degrader YJ1206. NF1 is a co-ablated tumor suppressor in the models, not the therapeutic target demonstrated here.

papers.title: A bedside-to-bench translational analysis of NF1 alterations and CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance in hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer.
papers.summary: The paper shows that pathogenic NF1 alterations identify a subset of hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancers with intrinsic or acquired resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors and worse clinical outcomes. NF1 knockout activates RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT signaling, while combined RAS or AKT inhibition—but not MEK or ERK inhibition—restores palbociclib activity in NF1-deficient cell lines and a patient-derived organoid.

papers.title: Oligodendrocyte RasG12V expressed in its endogenous locus disrupts myelin structure through increased MAPK, nitric oxide, and notch signaling.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of Costello syndrome, induction of endogenous HRasG12V in mature oligodendrocytes increased ERK activity and caused progressive myelin decompaction. MEK inhibition normalized g-ratio but did not significantly restore compaction alone; combined MEK and nitric-oxide synthase inhibition abolished myelin decompaction, supporting pathway-combination strategies downstream of abnormal Ras signaling.

papers.title: Mechanisms underlying cognitive deficits in a mouse model for Costello Syndrome are distinct from other RASopathy mouse models.
papers.summary: In HRas G12V/G12V mice, a model of Costello syndrome, MEK inhibition normalized elevated ERK signaling and rescued an mGluR-dependent long-term depression deficit, but it did not rescue spatial learning or brain hypertrophy. These results demonstrate that abnormal RAS-ERK activity can drive a specific synaptic phenotype through MEK while also showing that the cognitive and morphological abnormalities of this RASopathy require additional or developmentally earlier mechanisms.
papers.why: Tests pharmacologic rescue and a mechanistic synaptic endpoint in a RASopathy model, while showing that the cognitive mechanism and treatment response differ from NF1.

papers.title: Impact of MEK Inhibition on Childhood RASopathy-Associated Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: In a retrospective multicenter cohort of 61 children with RASopathy-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, off-label or compassionate use of the MEK inhibitor trametinib was associated with improved cardiac status and reduced cardiac surgery, transplantation, or death compared with standard care. The study supports MEK as a transferable therapeutic mechanism for RAS/MAPK-driven disease, particularly disease caused by activating germline variants, but does not establish randomized efficacy, optimal dosing, or long-term safety.

papers.title: Aberrant neuronal activity-induced signaling and gene expression in a mouse model of RASopathy.
papers.summary: In a forebrain-restricted Ptpn11D61Y mouse model of Noonan syndrome, neuronal activity failed to induce the normal increase in ERK phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, and activity-dependent gene-expression responses were strongly attenuated. The MEK inhibitor SL327 normalized basal nuclear pERK and restored activity-induced ERK phosphorylation, providing experimental evidence that MEK inhibition can correct a signaling defect downstream of overactive Ptpn11.

papers.title: <i>Mek1</i><sup>Y130C</sup> mice recapitulate aspects of human cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper establishes the Mek1Y130C mouse as a model of cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome and shows that MEK1 Y130C increases growth-factor-induced ERK phosphorylation despite reduced total MEK1 abundance. The mutant mice reproduce pulmonary artery stenosis, cranial dysmorphia, increased GFAP-positive astrocytes, increased Olig2-positive cells, and increased pERK-positive cells, linking CFC phenotypes to RAS/MAPK pathway hyperactivation.

papers.title: Exploring New Drug Repurposing Opportunities for MEK Inhibitors in RASopathies: A Comprehensive Review of Safety, Efficacy, and Future Perspectives of Trametinib and Selumetinib.
papers.summary: This review reports preclinical and clinical evidence that inhibiting MEK with trametinib, selumetinib, or PD0325901 can ameliorate RASopathy manifestations involving the heart, lymphatics, nervous system, growth, and other systems. Benefits were heterogeneous and sometimes transient or genotype-dependent, adverse events were common, and the evidence remains limited by retrospective case reports, short follow-up, publication bias, and the lack of standardized trials.

papers.title: Abrogation of Oncogenic RAS Signaling by a RAS(ON) Inhibitor Doublet Primes Immune-Refractory KRASG12C-Mutant NSCLC for Immune Checkpoint Blockade.
papers.summary: In KRASG12C-mutant non–small cell lung cancer models, combining active-state-selective elironrasib with multi-selective daraxonrasib produced deeper and more durable suppression of RAS signaling, enhanced antitumor activity, and delayed resistance compared with monotherapy. In immune-refractory, T cell–excluded 3LL-ΔNRAS tumors, the doublet increased antigen presentation and T-cell infiltration and enabled durable complete regressions when combined with anti–PD-1, providing a preclinical strategy that directly targets the RAS activation mechanism relevant to NF1 biology.

papers.title: The Multi-Level Mechanism of Action of a Pan-Ras Inhibitor Explains its Antiproliferative Activity on Cetuximab-Resistant Cancer Cells.
papers.summary: This paper shows that cmp4 is a pan-Ras inhibitor that acts at multiple steps of the Ras activation cycle, reducing intrinsic and GEF-mediated nucleotide exchange and Ras–Raf1 binding. In vitro experiments and mathematical modeling show antiproliferative activity across Ras mutants and cooperation with Cetuximab, although low affinity and possible off-target effects limit the current evidence for clinical application.

papers.title: Salirasib Inhibits the Expression of Genes Involved in Fibrosis in Fibroblasts of Systemic Sclerosis Patients.
papers.summary: In dermal fibroblasts from 10 patients with systemic sclerosis, the Ras inhibitor salirasib reduced H‐Ras expression, myofibroblast differentiation, and several profibrotic mediators while increasing MMP1 expression. These pilot in vitro findings support RAS activation as an actionable fibrosis mechanism, but most effects were measured at the mRNA level and require protein-level and functional validation.

papers.title: Spliceosomal mutation drives melanoma tumorigenesis via lineage-specific RAS activation.
papers.summary: The study shows that the SF3B1R625H hotspot causes preferential missplicing and nonsense-mediated decay of NF1, reducing neurofibromin and increasing RAS activation and RAS–MAPK signaling in melanoma models. NF1 restoration reverses MAPK activation, while the paper reports that direct evidence for MEK-inhibitor sensitivity remains lacking.

papers.title: Synthetic Lethal Interaction of SHOC2 Depletion with MEK Inhibition in RAS-Driven Cancers.
papers.summary: The paper identifies SHOC2 depletion or degradation as a potent, selective combination partner for MEK1/2 inhibition in RAS-driven cancer cells, suppressing adaptive RAF–MAPK reactivation and reducing proliferation and tumor growth. Genetic depletion, RNA interference, and a dTAG-mediated degrader all support the strategy, which was context-dependent and did not similarly sensitize cells to RAF inhibitors, gemcitabine, or a KRASG12C inhibitor.

papers.title: Multiselective RAS(ON) inhibition targets oncogenic RAS and overcomes RAS-mediated resistance to FLT3i and BCL2i in AML.
papers.summary: The paper shows that RMC-7977 inhibits active mutant and wild-type RAS in AML models, reverses resistance to FLT3 inhibition or venetoclax, and suppresses leukemic burden when combined with gilteritinib or venetoclax in patient-derived xenografts. These findings support clinical investigation of multiselective RAS(ON) inhibition for RAS-driven AML, but the evidence is preclinical.

papers.title: Spatially resolved transcriptomics of benign and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.
papers.summary: This pilot study applies spatial transcriptomics, network analysis, single-cell-data integration, and immunohistochemistry to benign and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (PNSTs). It identifies spatial transcriptional signatures, maps Schwann cell precursor and neural crest-like differentiation states in malignant PNST, and distinguishes hybrid PNSTs from pure and plexiform neurofibromas by the distribution of perineurial fibroblast markers; it reports no therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Upregulation of the Nr2f1-A830082K12Rik gene pair in murine neural crest cells results in a complex phenotype reminiscent of Waardenburg syndrome type 4.
papers.summary: The Spot mouse line models Waardenburg syndrome type 4 and Hirschsprung disease through derepression of the Nr2f1-A830082K12Rik gene pair in neural crest stem cell-derived enteric progenitors, causing premature gliogenesis, impaired intestinal colonization, and aganglionic megacolon. The study also identifies a conserved silencer element and provides fluorescent lineage labeling, enteric explant imaging, and 3C assays as mechanistic tools for studying neural crest stem cell defects, although it reports no therapeutic rescue and Nr2f1 sufficiency was supported by only one evaluable transgenic intestine.

papers.title: Ret deficiency decreases neural crest progenitor proliferation and restricts fate potential during enteric nervous system development.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: Single-cell profiling of Ret-deficient mouse enteric nervous system precursors shows that RET is required for neural crest stem cell/enteric neural crest–derived cell proliferation, migration, and access to an inhibitory-neuron developmental trajectory. The study provides a transferable developmental model and single-cell assay framework, but reports no therapeutic intervention or drug rescue for Hirschsprung disease or neurofibromatosis type 1.

papers.title: Identification of a neural development gene expression signature in colon cancer stem cells reveals a role for EGR2 in tumorigenesis.
papers.summary: In colorectal cancer, patient-derived organoids and xenografts show that ALDH-positive colon cancer stem cells acquire a neural-development state characterized by neural crest stem cell genes, with EGR2 maintaining an undifferentiated state through SOX2 and HOX genes. EGR2 knockdown reduced spheroid formation, proliferation, xenograft establishment, and tumor growth, suggesting targetable neural crest stem cell biology but not yet providing direct evidence in neurofibromatosis type 1.

papers.title: Epigenetic dynamics shaping melanophore and iridophore cell fate in zebrafish.
papers.summary: Comparative epigenomics of zebrafish neural crest-derived pigment cells identified enhancer-associated DNA methylation and chromatin accessibility dynamics that shape iridophore fate. Genetic loss-and-rescue experiments showed that alx4a is required for normal body iridophore differentiation and, together with gbx2, is sufficient to bias pigment progenitors toward an iridophore fate.

papers.title: Role of dual specificity phosphatases (DUSPs) in melanoma cellular plasticity and drug resistance.
papers.summary: This paper shows that melanoma cells with intrinsic or acquired resistance to BRAF or MEK inhibitors have reduced expression of the neural crest stem cell marker nestin, while DUSP1 and DUSP8 support their survival and resistance. Knockdown of DUSP1 or DUSP8, or pharmacological inhibition with BCI, restores MAPK-inhibitor sensitivity and can alter neural-lineage marker expression, but the findings are from melanoma cell-line models rather than neurofibromatosis type 1.

papers.title: A splice-switching oligonucleotide treatment ameliorates glycogen storage disease type 1a in mice with G6PC c.648G>T.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that the GalNAc-conjugated splice-switching oligonucleotide DS-4108b corrects aberrant G6PC c.648G>T splicing, restores glucose-6-phosphatase-α activity, and improves hepatic manifestations and fasting hypoglycemia in a humanized GSD1a mouse model. The work provides a transferable splice-correction strategy, but efficacy was predominantly hepatic and renal corrections were incomplete or not observed in some measures.

papers.title: Potential ASO-based personalized treatment for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2S.
papers.summary: The paper shows that a patient-specific 19-mer antisense oligonucleotide, VCA-894A, can skip a cryptic exon created by an IGHMBP2 intronic variant, restore IGHMBP2 expression, and improve neuromuscular-junction function in patient-derived CMT2S models. Intrathecal administration was well tolerated in wild-type Sprague-Dawley rats, supporting the general strategy of splice-modulating ASOs for cryptic intronic variants, although NF1 cryptic splicing was not studied directly.

papers.title: Cell modeling and rescue of a novel noncoding genetic cause of glycogen storage disease IX.
papers.summary: The study identifies and validates a deep intronic PHKG2 variant that creates a 76-bp pseudoexon and causes glycogen storage disease IX γ2, then uses CRISPR/Cas9-edited HEK293T cells to test splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides. Genome sequencing, RNA sequencing, and a personalized cell model provide a transferable workflow for detecting, modeling, and reversing cryptic-splicing defects, but the paper does not test or mention NF1 cryptic splicing or neurofibromatosis type 1.

papers.title: Antisense Oligonucleotide-Based Splice Correction of a Deep-Intronic Mutation in CHM Underlying Choroideremia.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that antisense oligonucleotides can correct the splice defect caused by the deep-intronic CHM variant c.315-4587T>A in patient-derived lymphoblast cells from individuals with choroideremia. The variant creates a novel splice acceptor and a 98-bp pseudoexon, providing a transferable splice-modulation strategy for deep-intronic mutations, although the study does not mention NF1 cryptic splicing.

papers.title: Antisense oligonucleotide induced pseudoexon skipping and restoration of functional protein for Fukuyama muscular dystrophy caused by a deep-intronic variant.
papers.summary: The study shows that an exonic splice enhancer-targeting antisense oligonucleotide can correct a deep-intronic FKTN variant in Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy by promoting pseudoexon skipping. In patient-derived cells, the intervention increased normal mRNA, restored FKTN protein production, and restored functional O-mannosyl glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan in myotubes.

papers.title: Exon-Skipping for a Pathogenic COL6A1 Variant in Ullrich Congenital Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: The paper describes an in vitro workflow for designing splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that skip a pathogenic deep-intronic COL6A1 pseudo-exon associated with Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy. It also outlines fibroblast transfection and qRT-PCR and western blot validation of splicing correction at the mRNA and protein levels.

unread.title: SPRED1 germline mutations caused a neurofibromatosis type 1 overlapping phenotype.
unread.why: Direct screening of an NF1-like cohort identified pathogenic SPRED1 variants and established their diagnostic value in the subset lacking NF1 mutations and neurofibromas.

unread.title: Location, symptoms, and management of plexiform neurofibromas in 127 children with neurofibromatosis 1, attending the National Complex Neurofibromatosis 1 service, 2018-2019.
unread.why: This same-disease pediatric cohort documents real-world use of MEK inhibitors, surgery, and conservative care together with clinically measurable plexiform-neurofibroma outcomes.

unread.title: Clinical and mutational spectrum of neurofibromatosis type 1-like syndrome.
unread.why: Large-scale testing and functional assays provide a validated diagnostic strategy for identifying SPRED1-related Legius syndrome among patients with NF1-like pigmentation but lacking characteristic tumors.

unread.title: Selumetinib Treatment in a Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Child With Second Hit Mutation on the NF1 Gene.
unread.why: This NF1 case reports rapid regression of inoperable plexiform neurofibromas with the MEK inhibitor selumetinib and identifies the tumor second-hit variant by sequencing.

unread.title: The diagnostic evaluation and multidisciplinary management of neurofibromatosis 1 and neurofibromatosis 2.
unread.why: This consensus review directly proposes diagnostic criteria and a comprehensive treatment and follow-up approach for NF1.

unread.title: Activity of Selumetinib in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Related Plexiform Neurofibromas.
unread.why: A phase 1 trial and mouse-model study demonstrate that selumetinib shrinks inoperable NF1 plexiform neurofibromas and establish a quantitative MRI response measure.

unread.title: Exhaustive mutation analysis of the NF1 gene allows identification of 95% of mutations and reveals a high frequency of unusual splicing defects.
unread.why: The study validates a multitechnique NF1 testing workflow that detects 95% of mutations in a well-characterized patient cohort.

unread.title: Mutation spectrum of NF1 gene in Italian patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 using Ion Torrent PGM™ platform.
unread.why: The study demonstrates a cost-effective sequencing and mosaicism-quantification workflow that identified NF1 variants in 79 Italian patients.

unread.title: Thirty-nine novel neurofibromatosis 1 (NF1) gene mutations identified in Slovak patients.
unread.why: The combined transcript-based sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis achieved a high NF1 detection rate and detected atypical splice defects missed by DNA-only testing.

unread.title: Mirdametinib: First Approval.
unread.why: Mirdametinib is an approved oral therapy for symptomatic, inoperable NF1-associated plexiform neurofibromas in adults and children.

unread.title: Recurrent NF1 gene variants and their genotype/phenotype correlations in patients with Neurofibromatosis type I.
unread.why: The cohort identifies recurrent NF1 variants, including p.Arg440*, p.Tyr489Cys, p.Arg1947*, and gross deletions, that are associated with higher complication rates and can inform genotype-informed stratification.

unread.title: Genetic diagnosis of neurofibromatosis type 1: targeted next- generation sequencing with Multiple Ligation-Dependent Probe Amplification analysis.
unread.why: The study validates a targeted sequencing plus MLPA workflow that identified NF1 and RAS-pathway variants and deletions in a 100-patient NF1 cohort.

unread.title: Isoform-specific NF1 mRNA levels correlate with disease severity in Neurofibromatosis type 1.
unread.why: The study shows in 138 NF1 patients that neurofibromin isoform I mRNA levels correlate with severe phenotypes and cognitive impairment, supporting an experimentally measured severity biomarker.

unread.title: Clinical Presentation and Novel Pathogenic Variants among 68 Chinese Neurofibromatosis 1 Children.
unread.why: Exome sequencing and Sanger confirmation identified pathogenic NF1 variants in 68 of 95 clinically suspected Chinese children and yielded genotype-phenotype data.

unread.title: Natural history of NF1 c.2970_2972del p.(Met992del): confirmation of a low risk of complications in a longitudinal study.
unread.why: Longitudinal follow-up of 41 carriers establishes a low-risk natural-history profile for p.Met992del that can support prognostication and counseling.

unread.title: Pediatric Diffuse Midline Gliomas H3 K27M-Mutant and Non-Histone Mutant Midline High-Grade Gliomas in Neurofibromatosis Type 1 in Comparison With Non-Syndromic Children: A Single-Center Pilot Study.
unread.why: This pilot study provides NF1-specific imaging characteristics and clinical PFS/OS data for pediatric midline high-grade gliomas.

unread.title: Brain injury drives optic glioma formation through neuron-glia signaling.
unread.why: The NF1 mouse experiments establish an injury-driven neuron–oligodendrocyte–microglia circuit and demonstrate suppression of glioma progression with inhibitors targeting that circuit.

unread.title: Clinical characteristics and mutation Spectrum of NF1 in 12 Chinese families with orbital/periorbital plexiform Neurofibromatosis type 1.
unread.why: NGS identified six novel NF1 mutations across 12 families and established mutation data relevant to the orbital/periorbital plexiform phenotype.

unread.title: Selumetinib use as targeted therapy for plexiform neurofibroma: a comprehensive review of the literature.
unread.why: The review summarizes targeted MEK inhibition with selumetinib for inoperable plexiform neurofibroma in NF1, directly documenting an established disease-specific treatment.

unread.title: Successful utilization of topical trametinib for neurofibromatosis type I-associated plexiform neurofibroma.
unread.why: This case reports topical trametinib producing more than two years of stability without systemic-treatment toxicities in an NF1-associated superficial plexiform neurofibroma.

unread.title: Toward More Accurate Diagnosis in Neurofibromatosis Type 1: A Dual-Level Analysis of Clinical and Molecular Data with Exploratory Genotype-Phenotype Correlations in a Romanian Cohort.
unread.why: The cohort demonstrates NF1 NGS testing, identifies clinically relevant variants, and proposes a resource-conscious diagnostic workflow for NF1.

unread.title: Selumetinib: the first ever approved drug for neurofibromatosis-1 related inoperable plexiform neurofibroma.
unread.why: The paper describes selumetinib’s regulatory approval and pivotal single-arm trial data, including approximately 70% partial tumor response and improvement in tumor-related complications.

unread.title: 10124-CS-11 Use of selumetinib in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 and concomitant plexiform neurofibroma and low-grade glioma: a report of two cases
unread.why: The title reports direct clinical use of selumetinib in two patients with NF1-associated plexiform neurofibroma and low-grade glioma, making it a disease-specific therapeutic solution despite the absent abstract.

unread.title: MEK inhibitors for neurofibromatosis type 1-associated central and peripheral nervous system tumors.
unread.why: The review consolidates clinical-trial evidence for MEK inhibitors in NF1-associated plexiform neurofibroma and low-grade glioma, including an approved selumetinib regimen.

unread.title: Neurofibromatosis type 1 molecular diagnosis: what can NGS do for you when you have a large gene with loss of function mutations?
unread.why: The study validates a high-throughput targeted NGS assay for NF1 diagnosis, including detection of mosaicism, tumor somatic mutations, and copy-number alterations.

unread.title: Durable Complete Response of a Recurrent Mesencephalic Glioblastoma Treated with Trametinib and Low-Dose Dabrafenib in a Patient with Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
unread.why: The NF1-associated glioblastoma patient achieved a durable complete response with combined MEK and BRAF inhibition, while dabrafenib also mitigated trametinib-related cutaneous toxicity.

unread.title: Expanding the Noonan spectrum/RASopathy NGS panel: Benefits of adding NF1 and SPRED1.
unread.why: Adding NF1 and SPRED1 to a RASopathy sequencing panel identified pathogenic variants in cohorts with suspected RASopathies, café-au-lait spots, or neurofibromatosis-Noonan phenotypes.

unread.title: Metalloproteinase 1 downregulation in neurofibromatosis 1: Therapeutic potential of antimalarial hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine.
unread.why: In NF1 patient-derived fibroblasts, hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine restored reduced MMP1 expression through AHR-dependent signaling and were proposed as neurofibroma therapies.

unread.title: Neurofibromin 1 mutations impair the function of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia.
unread.why: Engineered human iPSC-derived microglia carrying three patient NF1 mutations reproduced defective P2X signaling, phagocytosis, and motility.

unread.title: A major segment of the neurofibromatosis type 1 gene: cDNA sequence, genomic structure, and point mutations.
unread.why: The study established a major NF1 transcript and genomic structure and directly detected two pathogenic NF1 point mutations using PCR and sequencing.

unread.title: Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of individuals with neurofibromatosis 1.
unread.why: This consensus guideline defines practical diagnostic criteria, monitoring approaches, and management strategies for individuals with NF1.

unread.title: Selumetinib in Children with Inoperable Plexiform Neurofibromas.
unread.why: A phase II trial provides direct evidence that selumetinib produces durable tumor shrinkage and clinically meaningful symptom and functional benefit in children with NF1-associated inoperable plexiform neurofibromas.

unread.title: Prevalence of neurofibromatosis 1 in German children at elementary school enrollment.
unread.why: A large school-based screening study directly evaluates routine physical examination as a method for diagnosing most NF1 cases by age six.

unread.title: Astrocyte-specific inactivation of the neurofibromatosis 1 gene (NF1) is insufficient for astrocytoma formation.
unread.why: The study develops and experimentally characterizes a conditional mouse and astrocyte model specifically for NF1 loss and astrocytoma pathogenesis.

unread.title: Minor lesion mutational spectrum of the entire NF1 gene does not explain its high mutability but points to a functional domain upstream of the GAP-related domain.
unread.why: The large NF1 cohort study compares concrete mutation-screening methods and provides extensive mutation data and a map of functionally important NF1 regions.

unread.title: NF1 molecular characterization and neurofibromatosis type I genotype-phenotype correlation: the French experience.
unread.why: Reports a high-sensitivity NF1 molecular testing strategy combining transcript analysis, genomic sequencing, and MLPA for broad mutation detection.

unread.title: Extensive in silico analysis of NF1 splicing defects uncovers determinants for splicing outcome upon 5' splice-site disruption.
unread.why: Characterizes 94 pathogenic NF1 alterations and provides experimentally supported predictors of mutation-induced splicing outcomes and effective mutation detection.

unread.title: Nature and mRNA effect of 282 different NF1 point mutations: focus on splicing alterations.
unread.why: Reports a broad DNA/RNA mutation-testing workflow for 282 NF1 variants and quantifies how NF1 mutations alter transcript structure and splicing.

unread.title: Clinic-based study of plexiform neurofibromas in neurofibromatosis 1.
unread.why: Provides an 68-patient clinical series defining age of onset, distribution, morbidity, and malignant transformation outcomes for NF1 plexiform neurofibromas.

unread.title: A highly sensitive genetic protocol to detect NF1 mutations.
unread.why: A validated diagnostic protocol achieved 95% NF1 mutation sensitivity and was implemented routinely for detecting multiple mutation classes and copy-number changes.

unread.title: Elucidating the impact of neurofibromatosis-1 germline mutations on neurofibromin function and dopamine-based learning.
unread.why: Uses patient-derived cellular systems and engineered mice to link NF1 mutation dosage to neurofibromin function, RAS/cAMP signaling, dopamine levels, and learning phenotypes.

unread.title: Mutation spectrum of NF1 and clinical characteristics in 78 Korean patients with neurofibromatosis type 1.
unread.why: The study provides a comprehensive NF1 testing strategy and detailed mutation spectrum in Korean patients, making it directly reusable for molecular diagnosis and genetic counseling.

unread.title: Novel and recurrent mutations in the NF1 gene in Italian patients with neurofibromatosis type 1.
unread.why: Direct comparison of protein truncation testing and DHPLC provides an experimentally evaluated method for detecting NF1 mutations in affected patients.

unread.title: Phenotype categorization of neurofibromatosis type I and correlation to NF1 mutation types.
unread.why: The study develops an NF1+ clinical phenotype classification and shows that mutation type can stratify severe, earlier-onset disease, while supplying a large genotype-phenotype dataset.

unread.title: Exon 10b of the NF1 gene represents a mutational hotspot and harbors a recurrent missense mutation Y489C associated with aberrant splicing.
unread.why: The study establishes exon 10b as a recurrent mutational hotspot, characterizes Y489C-associated exon skipping, and proposes prioritizing this exon in NF1 mutation analysis.

unread.title: Moyamoya syndrome in children with neurofibromatosis type 1: Italian-French experience.
unread.why: The study supports adding cerebral angiography to pediatric NF1 brain MRI and provides clinical and radiological criteria that may facilitate early moyamoya diagnosis.

unread.title: SPRED 1 mutations in a neurofibromatosis clinic.
unread.why: SPRED1 sequencing distinguishes Legius syndrome from NF1 in phenotypically overlapping patients and supports surveillance tailored to the absence of tumor manifestations.

unread.title: Human induced pluripotent stem cell engineering establishes a humanized mouse platform for pediatric low-grade glioma modeling.
unread.why: Engineered hiPSC-derived pediatric low-grade glioma lines carrying NF1 loss establish a reproducible humanized model and show therapeutic activity of the MEK inhibitor PD0325901 in vitro and in vivo.

unread.title: NF1 gene analysis based on DHPLC.
unread.why: The study establishes DHPLC conditions covering all NF1 coding exons and splice junctions and demonstrates a 72.5% mutation detection rate.

unread.title: Accurate Classification of NF1 Gene Variants in 84 Italian Patients with Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
unread.why: Comprehensive computational analysis identified splice-disrupting NF1 variants and phenotype-associated variant classes that can improve molecular diagnosis and patient characterization.

unread.title: Functional analysis of splicing mutations in exon 7 of NF1 gene.
unread.why: Bioinformatic mapping and minigene experiments revealed splice-regulatory elements and distinguished the splicing effects of three NF1 exon 7 variants.

unread.title: Neurofibromin (NF1) genetic variant structure-function analyses using a full-length mouse cDNA.
unread.why: The heterologous full-length Nf1 cDNA system functionally tests patient variants for neurofibromin production and rescue of Ras signaling in NF1-null cells.

unread.title: Hybrid Minigene Assay: An Efficient Tool to Characterize mRNA Splicing Profiles of NF1 Variants.
unread.why: The validated minigene system rapidly characterized 29 NF1 variants, identified multiple splice-altering mechanisms, and detected hypomorphic effects without requiring patient RNA.

unread.title: Unidentified bright objects associated with features of neurofibromatosis 1.
unread.why: In 523 patients with NF1, MRI-visible unidentified bright objects were quantified and statistically associated with optic glioma and other cardinal NF1 features, supporting their use as a measurable marker.

unread.title: Identification of an atypical microdeletion generating the RNF135-SUZ12 chimeric gene and causing a position effect in an NF1 patient with overgrowth.
unread.why: The study uses array CGH, long-range PCR, transcript analysis, and expression measurements to resolve an atypical NF1 microdeletion and its position effect.

unread.title: Clinical and Molecular Characterization of NF1 Patients: Single-Center Experience of 32 Patients From China.
unread.why: The authors developed and tested a combined DNA/cDNA sequencing, MLPA, and segregation-analysis protocol that detected NF1 mutations in 93.8% of 32 patients.

unread.title: Modulation of aberrant NF1 pre-mRNA splicing by kinetin treatment.
unread.why: Kinetin partially corrected four distinct NF1 pre-mRNA splicing defects in patient-derived cell lines, providing an experimentally tested compound and assay despite its stated therapeutic limitations.

unread.title: MEK inhibition ameliorates social behavior phenotypes in a Spred1 knockout mouse model for RASopathy disorders.
unread.why: Acute MEK inhibition reversed abnormal social dominance and improved nesting in a RASopathy mouse model, demonstrating a mechanistically transferable approach to behavioral NF1 phenotypes.

unread.title: High-Grade Astrocytoma with Piloid Features: A Dual Institutional Review of Imaging Findings of a Novel Entity.
unread.why: The study characterizes MRI, molecular, and clinical features of high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features and identifies imaging or underlying NF1 findings as diagnostic cues.

unread.title: Congenital glaucoma and neurofibromatosis in a monozygotic twin: case report and review of the literature.
unread.why: The case and literature review support targeted early NF1 assessment, including neural-axis imaging, in newborns presenting with unilateral congenital glaucoma.

unread.title: Clinical characteristics and spectrum of NF1 mutations in 12 unrelated Chinese families with neurofibromatosis type 1.
unread.why: A combined sequencing and MLPA strategy identified recurrent and novel NF1 variants in 12 families, while clinical imaging and follow-up documented associated phenotypes.

unread.title: Simultaneous Detection of NF1, SPRED1, LZTR1, and NF2 Gene Mutations by Targeted NGS in an Italian Cohort of Suspected NF1 Patients.
unread.why: The validated NGS-plus-MLPA strategy detected NF1 and phenotypically overlapping RASopathy/schwannomatosis gene variants, with RNA sequencing recovering variants missed by genomic NGS.

unread.title: Affinity Purification of NF1 Protein-Protein Interactors Identifies Keratins and Neurofibromin Itself as Binding Partners.
unread.why: The paper establishes functional NF1 affinity-purification and interactomics methods that identify neurofibromin binding partners and can support discovery of Ras-independent drug targets.

unread.title: Eighteen-year survival of a patient with malignant pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma associated with von Recklinghausen neurofibromatosis.
unread.why: An NF1-associated malignant pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma was treated with total resection and radiation, with reported tumor-free survival for 18 years.

unread.title: Manifestations and Treatment of Adult-onset Symptomatic Optic Pathway Glioma in Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
unread.why: The report provides an NF1-specific treatment case in which adjusted carboplatin chemotherapy improved visual function in symptomatic adult optic pathway glioma.

unread.title: Selumetinib normalizes Ras/MAPK signaling in clinically relevant neurofibromatosis type 1 minipig tissues in vivo.
unread.why: The NF1 minipig study directly demonstrates selumetinib exposure, ERK-pathway pharmacodynamic effects, and tissue biomarkers relevant to plexiform neurofibroma and CNS tumor research.

unread.title: Neurofibromatosis 1 (von Recklinghausen Disease).
unread.why: This NF1-focused review identifies a clinically established MEK1/2 inhibitor for inoperable symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas and describes diagnostic testing and disease-monitoring practices.

unread.title: Insights into Novel Choroidal and Retinal Clinical Signs in Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
unread.why: The review reports specific ocular imaging, electrophysiology, and revised diagnostic criteria for detecting and characterizing NF1-related manifestations.

unread.title: A rare vulvar manifestation of neurofibromatosis 1 in a teen.
unread.why: This case provides disease-specific clinical evidence for treating a symptomatic vulvar neurofibroma with surgical excision.

unread.title: Clinical characteristics and genetic testing outcome of suspected hereditary peripheral nerve sheath tumours in a tertiary cancer institution in Singapore.
unread.why: The study reports a clinical and genetic testing pathway for hereditary peripheral nerve sheath tumors and provides NF1 diagnostic outcomes in a real-world cohort.

unread.title: Gene diagnosis of infantile neurofibromatosis type I: A case report.
unread.why: The case provides disease-specific evidence for early NF1 recognition, imaging and gene-based confirmation, and management/prognostic assessment in infantile disease.

unread.title: Rare NF1 microdeletion syndrome in an Omani patient.
unread.why: The case shows that chromosomal microarray/CGH can identify a de novo 17q11.2 deletion causing an NF1 phenotype with additional Noonan-like features.

unread.title: Longitudinal Assessment of Enhancing Foci of Abnormal Signal Intensity in Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
unread.why: The longitudinal NF1 study establishes MRI follow-up and lesion-volume change as practical outcome and diagnostic measures for evaluating enhancing brain lesions.

unread.title: Perspectives of adolescents with neurofibromatosis 1 and cutaneous neurofibromas: Implications for clinical trials.
unread.why: This NF1-specific study provides validated patient-centered outcome measures and registry-based methods for designing cutaneous neurofibroma clinical trials.

unread.title: Targeted Therapies in Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
unread.why: The paper identifies selumetinib and mirdametinib as approved targeted treatments for inoperable symptomatic or progressive plexiform neurofibromas and describes additional MEK inhibitors under clinical investigation.

unread.title: Pediatric Optic Pathway Gliomas: A Report From Northern Greece.
unread.why: This NF1-associated optic pathway glioma cohort reports real-world use of chemotherapy, surgery, surveillance, tumor staging, and long-term clinical outcomes.

unread.title: Case Report: Mosaicism of a novel nonsense variant in the neurofibromin gene underlies a mosaic generalized NF1 phenotype.
unread.why: The study uses both next-generation and Sanger sequencing to identify and quantify a previously unreported mosaic NF1 nonsense variant in a patient with generalized mosaic NF1.

unread.title: Inhibition of Cxcr4 chemokine receptor signaling improves habituation learning and increases cAMP-PKA signaling in a zebrafish model of Neurofibromatosis type 1.
unread.why: The study tests plerixafor in an NF1 mutant zebrafish model and reports improved habituation learning through CXCR4 inhibition and cAMP-PKA pathway activation.

unread.title: Metabolic and behavioral effects of neurofibromin result from differential recruitment of MAPK and mTOR signaling.
unread.why: The paper experimentally identifies distinct MEK-dependent behavioral and MEK/mTOR-dependent metabolic mechanisms in a genetically tractable Drosophila NF1 model.

unread.title: Neurofibromatosis Type 1 in Ecuador: genotype-phenotype correlations from a case series.
unread.why: The NF1 case series demonstrates mutation detection and interpretation using a cancer NGS panel, standardized pathogenicity classifiers, and ancestry analysis.
